critical_code_review_comments: backend/models/task.py FollowupIn requires `task_id` in request body but the endpoint /api/v1/tasks/{task_id}/followups already takes task_id from path — the body field is redundant and forces clients to send the id twice. Consider dropping task_id from FollowupIn.

backend/routers/vendor_auth.py silently lowercases email on lookup but registrations/approval flow may not enforce lowercase on insert (in our test we had to lowercase manually because the vendor was originally inserted with uppercase TEST_). Verify _seed vendor from registration.approve inserts lowercase — otherwise login will fail forever for those vendors. RCA below.
server.py still uses deprecated @app.on_event('startup') — migrate to lifespan context manager.

bids.py POST /decision compares `admin['role']` to `payload.role` with a special-case for committee_member↔committee — brittle string match, easy to break. Extract into a helper `roles_match(active_role, action_role)`.

committee.py — `admin['id'] not in ({chair, *members})` set contains stringified ObjectIds; if any id has extra whitespace or case-diff (unlikely but possible from client), membership check fails silently as 403. Consider normalising in a shared util.
payments.py refund endpoint calls stripe.Refund.create synchronously inside async endpoint — this blocks the event loop; wrap in `await run_in_threadpool`. Not tested end-to-end.
committee.py auto-adds committee_member role to referenced staff on create — harmless but not audit-logged individually. Fine for Wave 1.
No index on vendors.email (unique) — duplicate approvals could create two vendor logins for the same email. Add unique index.

rca of the issue: During initial test run, vendor login returned 401 despite the vendor row + bcrypt hash being present in db.vendors and verify_password returning True in a standalone Python check. Root cause: vendor_auth.vendor_login lowercases `payload.email.lower()` before the DB lookup, but the test fixture inserted the vendor with uppercase prefix `TEST_vendor_...@example.com`. Since MongoDB find is case-sensitive, the query missed the document → 401. Fix: use lowercase email in the seeded vendor. Broader concern: the real approval flow in registrations.py inserts `doc['email']` directly (whatever case the user typed on the registration form); if a supplier registers with mixed-case email, subsequent login will silently fail. Recommend either lowercasing at insert (registrations.py:216-224) OR making the vendor find_one case-insensitive via a regex/collation.
